TensorFlow Recommenders implements precomputed candidate embeddings through `factorized_top_k.BruteForce.index_from_dataset`; the equivalent PyTorch implementation caches a fused item matrix E and scores `features @ E.T`, chunking the catalog when necessary. This applies to HSTU when item fusion depends only on item ID/text and trained parameters; user-dependent gates cannot be cached globally. Exact matrix scoring preserves full-catalog scores; approximate retrieval can change rankings. [TFRS implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/recommenders/blob/main/tensorflow_recommenders/layers/factorized_top_k.py).

Recommended design: one differentiable `encode_items(ids)` shared by history encoding, target scoring, diagnostics and cache construction. For residual fusion, use `e_id + has_text * sigmoid(gate) * projected_text`; mask after projection so biases cannot create text contributions for missing metadata. Exclude padded tokens from text pooling, clamp pooling denominators, and explicitly zero item-padding vectors after fusion/normalization. `padding_idx=0` protects the ID lookup’s padding gradient, but does not mask subsequent transformations. With left-padded histories, read the final nonpadding position. Apply identical normalization order, dimensions, epsilon, temperature and item biases everywhere. These are implementation recommendations grounded in [PyTorch embedding semantics](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/sparse.py) and [normalization semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.normalize.html).

Build the cache after loading the selected checkpoint, with `model.eval()` and `torch.inference_mode()`; inference mode alone does not disable dropout. Rebuild after parameter, metadata or vocabulary changes; never reuse detached fused embeddings across training updates. Keep category caches checkpoint-specific and update the embedded predictor writer. Verify cached versus uncached evaluation scores within floating-point tolerance, including missing-text items and padding; stochastic training scores are not expected to match evaluation scores. [PyTorch inference-mode documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode.html).
